# NPM Improved v1.6.15 — Complete October 2026 Security Update + Reinstall Recovery

**Important security maintenance. Upgrade existing installations to v1.6.15.**

This release contains the **entire security bundle** originally consolidated under v1.6.14, while giving existing v1.6.14 installations a **newer version** that the built-in updater will recognize. You only need to upgrade once: **v1.6.15 includes all the security fixes**, not just the newest one.

## Security fixes included

### NGINX 1.31.8 — public reverse proxy

The running NGINX proxy executable is updated to version **1.31.8**. This incorporates fixes for five October 2026 security advisories:

- CVE-2026-15176: `alias`/`rewrite` buffer overflow
- CVE-2026-93479: script/variable-evaluation buffer overflow
- CVE-2026-97205: SSI / asynchronous-I/O use-after-free
- CVE-2026-95101: HTTP/3 request-body injection
- CVE-2026-97629: TLS session-ticket-key forgery

Matching GeoIP2 HTTP and stream dynamic modules are rebuilt and verified against the exact NGINX source release.

### Node.js 24.22.1 — application and management API

Installs the actual **Node.js 24.22.1** runtime in the production image, incorporating the October 21 security fixes, including TLS hostname-verification and DNS parsing issues. The release build checks the executable inside the final container, not only the declared package version.

### Go 1.27.3 — native control plane

Rebuilds the native control-plane executable using **Go 1.27.3**, incorporating the October 19 crypto/x509 security update (CVE-2026-111943). Retains its required restricted-user listener capabilities.

## New: Reinstall Current Release

A new **Settings → Update → Maintenance & Recovery → Reinstall Current Release** action lets administrators intentionally reapply the **latest stable release published on GitHub**, **even when the same version number is already installed**.

- Requires the current administrator password and refreshes official GitHub release metadata before starting.
- Downloads the published architecture-specific GitHub Release image bundle with SHA-256 verification, falling back to the official GHCR image if needed.
- Reuses the native host updater for the same migration/restore/NPMX safeguards, health checks, and automatic rollback as an ordinary update.
- On same-version reinstall, snapshots the existing image by its actual immutable image ID before repulling a reused version tag. A failed reinstall can therefore restore the previous image.
- Reapplies the checksum-verified host updater itself even when the release number has not changed.
- Preserves proxy hosts, passwords, certificates, volumes, database settings, ports, and NPMX pairing.

This is a **manual recovery action**, not an automatic same-version refresh. A separate host-updater upgrade may be needed for older installations before the option is enabled.

## Upgrading from v1.6.14

1. Back up persistent NPMi data and certificate volumes.
2. Use **Settings → Update** to install **v1.6.15**. Unlike the previously reissued v1.6.14 image, v1.6.15 is visible to the normal version checker.
3. For NPMX clusters, upgrade the secondary node first, validate health and HTTPS traffic, then upgrade the primary. Confirm NPMX synchronization returns to healthy status.
4. Check **Settings → Update → Maintenance & Recovery** for the new **Reinstall Current Release** control once the native host updater has refreshed.
5. Verify your running image contains **NGINX 1.31.8**, **Node.js 24.22.1** and the newly compiled Go control plane.

## Compatibility and release verification

No intentional change to proxy-host configuration, admin permissions, update rollback contract, database schema, or the NPMX sync protocol. Custom OpenResty/Lua extensions still require review because the proxy executable is now standard NGINX.

AMD64/ARM64 Docker images and verified release bundles are available. Release checks validate the actual patched runtimes, rebuilt modules, backend/frontend tests, native updater, NPMX pairing, and database migrations.
